clue.text: Spirited company Robin organised

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters of the name are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A lively firm run by someone named Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges ROBIN to NBRIO, which follows CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Con brio is a musical direction meaning with vigour, so it describes a spirited performance.

clue.text: Crown right one lying abed

indicators.note: lying, read with abed, says these pieces are laid down within the bed

parts.note: abed points to a bed, here a cot

explanation.surface: Someone lazing in bed is told their crown is right there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' puts R and ONE inside COT, the bed that 'abed' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by nobles.

clue.text: Of western remade in which ponies may be seen

definitions.text: in which ponies may be seen

indicators.note: remade says the letters of the two words are made up again in another order

explanation.surface: A Western film being remade with ponies on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remade' rearranges OF WESTERN. The NEW FOREST is a national park in Hampshire, England, famous for its free-roaming ponies.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Forest is a stretch of English heathland known for its wild ponies.

clue.text: Spoke more than once?

parts.note: reads as having talked repeatedly, but spoke is the noun, a wheel's rod, and more than once asks for its plural

explanation.definitionFit: Radii is the plural of radius, a straight line from a centre, which is what the spokes of a wheel are.

clue.text: Holm-oak disquieted an American

indicators.note: disquieted means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An American unsettled by a holm-oak tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disquieted' rearranges HOLMOAK to OKLAHOM; AN follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oklahoman is a native of the US state of Oklahoma, so an American.

clue.text: Make wider path through mountain

indicators.note: through says one piece runs inside the other

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a path or way

explanation.surface: Widening a track that passes through a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' puts ROAD inside BEN, a Scottish word for a mountain (Ben Nevis).
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden something is to make it wider or more extensive.

clue.text: Essential bit of kebab as I chew

indicators.note: bit of says the letters come from a part of the following run of words

explanation.surface: Someone eating a kebab declares one piece essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' picks the letters running across keBAB AS I Chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental, the essential part of something.

clue.text: Domestic support for alumnus on the look-out

indicators.note: in a down clue, support for puts the second piece beneath the first

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
a domestic is a household servant

explanation.surface: Household help assisting a former student who is keeping watch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'support for' puts SERVANT under OB (old boy, a school's former pupil).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant is watchful, always on the look-out.

clue.text: Dream about the true skin

indicators.note: about here means around in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dreaming about what lies beneath your skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The derma, or dermis, is the layer of skin beneath the epidermis, once called the true skin.

clue.text: Actor Paul accepting lead in Sandler's Ed

indicators.note: accepting says the actor's surname takes something inside it

parts.note: Paul Newman was a Hollywood actor

indicators.note: lead in means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Paul Newman takes a part as a character called Ed in an Adam Sandler film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts S, from 'lead in' Sandler's, inside NEWMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed is short for editor, a journalist in charge of a paper, a kind of newsman.

clue.text: Maybe king due favour had tiff

parts.note: R is short for Rex, king, as on coins
a person due a favour is owed one

explanation.surface: A king expecting a return favour falls out with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: R is Rex, Latin for king. Rowed here rhymes with 'loud': a British word for quarrelled.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use, to row is to quarrel, so rowed means had a tiff or argument.

clue.text: Endure return of verrucae? Too much for patient

parts.note: to last is to endure

indicators.note: return of says the following word's synonym is read backwards

parts.note: verrucae are warts on the foot

explanation.surface: A patient with returning verrucae has finally had enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns WARTS round to STRAW, after LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw is the final thing that exhausts someone's patience, an idiom from the straw that broke the camel's back.

clue.text: Compiler brightened this classical old age

parts.note: Neo is the setter of this puzzle, the compiler
lit means brightened
hic is Latin, the classical tongue, for this

explanation.surface: The puzzle's author lit up this ancient era.
explanation.walkthrough: Compiler refers to the setter, Neo. HIC is Latin for 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic is the New Stone Age, a prehistoric era.

clue.text: Silver coin Mike found in kingdom

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish silver coin
Mike is the radio code word for M

explanation.surface: A man named Mike finds a silver coin in a kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The real was a silver coin in Spain; Mike is M in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the domain of a monarch.

clue.text: Bit of a shock — tension initially relieved

indicators.note: initially relieved says the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: stress is tension

explanation.surface: A small shock eases the stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially relieved' drops the first S of STRESS. A shock here is a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock of hair, a piece of a shock of hair.

clue.text: Grand (US) raised by mysterious stalker

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upward, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
arcane means mysterious

explanation.surface: A grand American sum held aloft by a shadowy stalker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns G and US round to SUG in a down clue, above ARCANE. The definition jokes that the plant has stalks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugarcane is a tall grass with a thick stalk, playfully called a stalker.

clue.text: People in serious offence

parts.note: mortals are people, humans

explanation.surface: People involved in a serious crime.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a mortal sin is a grave sin, a serious offence against God.

clue.text: Given hope on the river, fool dons purple

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the piece is covered by the colour

parts.note: purple shades to red

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: an ass is a fool
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A fool by the river puts on purple and is comforted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets ASS above URE, a Yorkshire river; 'dons' puts that inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reassured is to have doubts removed and confidence or hope restored.

clue.text: Mark given in development of master plan

indicators.note: given in says one piece is placed inside the other
development of says the word is worked into a new form

parts.note: a tag is a mark or label

explanation.surface: A grand scheme developed with a mark added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' turns MASTER into STRAEM; 'given in' puts TAG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or scheme.

clue.text: Secretary off again to land of giants

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: off means awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A secretary sets off again for a land of giants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges AGAIN TO into TAGONIA, after PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Early European explorers told of giants living in Patagonia, a region of southern South America.

clue.text: Desire held in by salesperson?

indicators.note: held in says the desire is kept within the other piece

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
an itch is a desire

explanation.surface: A salesperson keeping a longing in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' puts ITCH inside PER. The question mark marks a playful definition: one who makes a sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller who makes a sales pitch might whimsically be called a pitcher.

clue.text: Sound of the Bull Ring

indicators.note: Sound of says the word is said aloud and the letters follow its pronunciation

parts.note: Taurus is the Bull of the zodiac

explanation.surface: The noise from the bull ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Taurus, the Bull, said aloud gives the spelling TORUS. 'Bull Ring' suggests a bullfighting arena, but Ring is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a ring-shaped solid, like a doughnut.

clue.text: Barber of Suffolk and Kent, say

definitions.text: Barber of Suffolk and Kent, say

parts.words: Barber of Suffolk and Kent, say
parts.note: seems to be a hairdresser working in two English counties, but Suffolk and Kent are breeds of sheep

explanation.definitionFit: A shearer cuts the fleece of sheep, such as the Suffolk and Kent breeds, like a barber.

clue.text: British in line with flower of Rome

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tier is a line or row

explanation.surface: A British gardener lines up with a Roman bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B inside TIER. A 'flower' in crosswords can be a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river that flows through Rome; a river is a flower in the sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Explosion yet to catch disheartened rebels

indicators.note: to catch says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: but means yet

indicators.note: disheartened means with the heart, the middle letters, removed

explanation.surface: An explosion has yet to trap discouraged rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves RS from rebels; 'to catch' puts that inside BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst is a sudden explosion or outbreak.

clue.text: X marks spot under this, the death of Balder

definitions.meaning: X is a kiss, marking the spot under a sprig hung at Christmas
in Norse myth the god Balder was killed by a dart made from this plant

explanation.walkthrough: X stands for a kiss: the line sounds like a treasure map but points to kissing under the sprig.
explanation.definitionFit: People kiss under this plant at Christmas, and in Norse myth a dart of it killed the god Balder.

clue.text: Musical piece with bubbly timekeeping!

indicators.note: keeping says the champagne holds the other piece inside

parts.note: Moet is a brand of champagne, bubbly

explanation.surface: Champagne served while a piece of music keeps time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' sits inside the word timekeeping, whose front half supplies T: time keeping T inside MOET, the champagne house.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, usually sacred.

clue.text: Permission to go

definitions.meaning: permission, as in being granted time off

explanation.definitionFit: Leave means permission as in shore leave, and to depart or go away.

clue.text: 3 fear transition to life beyond

indicators.note: transition means change, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: the figure 3 is written out as a word

explanation.surface: A fear of change leading to the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transition' rearranges THREE and FEAR. 3 looks like a cross-reference to another clue but is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereafter is the life after death.

clue.text: Reason for seeing red interior of Range Rover

indicators.note: interior of says the letters are inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something red inside the Range Rover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior of' picks the letters inside rANGE Rover.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is what makes someone see red, an idiom for becoming furious.

clue.text: Back-to front sort of departure?

parts.note: seems to describe a reversed exit, but describes an army going back from the front line

explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a withdrawal of troops backward, away from the front.

clue.text: Paper in German for the idealist

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: der is German for the
a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper in German appealing to the idealist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts REAM inside DER, German for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is an idealist, someone with lofty unrealistic hopes.
